files.why: Date-range picker widget duplicated into billing's ui/ (rule 7: only 2 usages -> duplicate, do not promote to shared/ until a 3rd same-reason use; worked example #3).
Render the filter above the invoices table and bind the selected range.
Own the selected-range ref and filter the invoice list by it (client-side; the store already loads all invoices, so no data-layer change here).
A separate copy of the same widget in scheduling's ui/ — same look but a distinct reason to change, so duplicated rather than shared (rules 6 and 7).
Render the filter at the top and replace the fixed single `day` ref with the selected range.
Accept a date range instead of a single `day: Ref<Date>` and drive fetching/filtering from it.
Add a range query (e.g. fetchAppointmentsInRange); the existing fetchAppointmentsForDay only covers a single day.

uncertain: Duplicate-per-slice vs one shared/ui primitive: the phrase 'same look and behaviour in both' pushes toward a single shared/ui/date-range-picker/, but the constitution (rule 7 + worked example #3) says duplicate at 2 usages and only promote at the 3rd. I followed the constitution (duplicated); a team could reasonably decide this is a design-system primitive from day one.
Whether scheduling truly needs the data/queries.ts change or could filter client-side in the composable the way billing does via its store — depends on API/data volume; I assumed a new range query.

If a DateRange {start,end} value type is extracted, where it lives: slice-ui-local vs shared/lib. Slice roots allow only core/data/ui/routes.ts/index.ts, so I kept the range shape local to each component/composable rather than inventing a home for it.

Whether to add composable unit tests for the new filtering behaviour: the repo currently has only core/mappers tests (no composable/view tests), so there is no precedent to match, and I did not list speculative test files.
questions: Which date should the invoice list filter on — the invoice's own issueDate, or the 'Generated from' appointment start it currently displays (from scheduling)? They can differ, and the second would filter on cross-slice data.

The current scheduling screen is a single-day view; does a date-range filter turn it into a multi-day range view, and if so how should cross-day conflict detection (findConflicts, currently computed per day) behave across the range?
Is 'same look and behaviour' a directive to ship ONE shared component (accepting a rule-7 exception), or just a UX-consistency requirement that two matching duplicates satisfy?
Should the selected range persist in the URL/query params (shareable/bookmarkable) or is component-local state acceptable?
What is the default range on load (e.g. current month, or the existing fixed demo day), and does an empty/unset range mean 'show all'?
